title: A notebook runs out of memory: collect() on a large table and a skewed join
objective_text: Read the symptoms of a driver overload and a skewed join, and choose the cause and the fix for each.
scenario: A nightly notebook first failed when it pulled a whole table into Python, and after that was patched, its join to customers crawled on one task. The team needs to know what Spark does and what to change.
verifies: You can pick the right feature, setting or operator for each scenario, with the reason and source shown afterwards.
does_not_verify: That you can do it in Fabric: nothing is set up or run here. Doing it on a real item is FABRIC VERIFIED work.

validation.fail: Not all right yet: reread the lesson's notes and try again.

explanation: Each question's answer, reason and source page are shown after a pass or on request.
review_notes: Every claim was checked against its source page on 2026-11-07.

Sources read 2026-11-07: pyspark-pandas-conversion (toPandas collects all records to the driver, use a small subset), Azure Databricks aqe (AQE on by default; splits skewed tasks in sort merge and shuffle hash joins; skewed = more than 5 x median and more than 256MB), Synapse apache-spark-performance (autoBroadcastJoinThreshold or join(broadcast(df2))), Fabric spark-monitor-debug (Spark advisor skew detection). The AQE facts come from Databricks' page and match Apache Spark's own tuning guide; Fabric's runtime may set its own defaults. The notes' line about collect() follows Apache Spark's documentation, which isn't on Learn, so no question rests on it.
